findings: **The radar's dirty check holds: a frame where nothing moved costs ZERO canvas calls.** Not 'few' — the layer returns before touching the context. At 60 fps over a still map with a 20 Hz board that is 20 repaints a second instead of 60, and over a console nobody is touching it is none, which is the shape chain 4 needs rather than something to retrofit.

**One repaint is 914 calls at the declared worst case** (150 units, 40 calls, a 160-box city). The largest single contributor is the district outline — 160 `rect` calls in one path — and it is the part that never changes; caching it to an offscreen canvas is priced in `docs/performance/deferred-optimizations/radar-outline-cache.md` and deliberately not taken while the repaint is already conditional.

**Ten annotations cost 422 calls, 42 per shape of eight points.** They are drawn every frame the overlay is drawn, because they sit on the symbology canvas with the chips — so this is the number that has to stay small, and it is roughly one call per point plus the halo/label pair.

The counts are not comparable to [5/02's symbology census](2026-08-21-dispatch-symbology-call-counts.json), which counted three specific call KINDS (`fillText`, `measureText`, font assignments) rather than every call. Both are stub-context desk counts; neither is a timing.
note: WHAT THE CONSOLE'S TWO NEW 2D LAYERS ASK OF THE CANVAS (201/7-04 the radar, 201/7-05 the sketches). A DESK COUNT, not a timing: the layers are driven with a stub 2D context that records calls. Board 150 units + 40 calls, 160 district boxes, 10 sketches of 8 points, radar 132 CSS px. Instrument: `scripts/debug/overlay-census.ts`. Milliseconds are owed by 2/03's device run — this says how much work is requested, never how long a browser takes to do it.
openQuestions: What 914 calls a repaint costs in milliseconds on a Mali-G51. A 132 px dial is a small surface, but 2D canvas on a phone is where this console's frame budget has been surprised before (overlay-2d at 2.44 ms drawing nine units).

Whether an operator wants the radar at all zoom levels. It frames the WHOLE world, so at block zoom the footprint polygon is a few pixels — legible as a position, useless as a shape. A second scale (the district box) is the obvious answer and nobody has asked for it yet.
